note: Which declarations give an export its parameters, and the parser's edge cases. A declaration gives the parameters of the export of its name; anything else has an empty list (ADR 0002).

cases.title: an arrow main gets an empty parameter list
cases.rest_in: C3a calls it with no arguments

cases.title: a script without a main export records only what it exports
cases.rest_in: C3a fails the step with main function is missing

cases.title: a destructured parameter is named anon1
cases.rest_in: C3a binds it from the args key anon1 (WR-7/c and WR-7/d)

given.source: export function main({ a }: { a: number }) { return a; }

cases.title: destructured parameters are numbered in order, a destructured default included

given.source: export function main(a, { b }: { b: number }, { c } = { c: 1 }) { return [a, b, c]; }

cases.note: The reference numbers destructured parameters in order; that a named parameter does not take a number and that a destructured parameter with a default is one too are this build's reading (open question in the PR).

cases.title: a rest parameter of a declaration makes the parse fail for that export
cases.note: The text after the colon is free text (…) in the reference.

given.source:
export function main(...xs: number[]) { return xs.length; }
export function other(a: number) { return a; }

cases.title: an array-destructuring parameter is one of the other unsupported patterns
cases.note: The reference names object destructuring (anonN) and the rest parameter; this build reads array destructuring as another unsupported pattern. Open question in the PR.

given.source: export function main([a, b]: number[]) { return a + b; }

cases.title: a declaration exported later by name gives the export its parameters

given.source:
function main(a: number, b: string) { return [a, b]; }
export { main };

cases.title: an export renamed from another declaration has no declaration of its own name

given.source:
function helper(a: number) { return a; }
export { helper as main };

cases.title: export default function main is exported as default, which no declaration names

given.source: export default function main(a: number) { return a; }

cases.title: a const holding a function expression is not a declaration

given.source: export const main = async function (a: number) { return a; };
export async function main(a: number = 1, b?: string) { return [a, b]; }

cases.title: a TypeScript this parameter is not a parameter at run time
cases.note: TypeScript erases a this parameter; the reference does not cover it. Open question in the PR.

given.source: export function main(this: unknown, a: number) { return a; }

cases.title: of an overloaded declaration, the first signature counts
cases.note: The reference does not cover overloads. Open question in the PR.

given.source:
export function main(a: Date): string;
export function main(b: any) { return String(b); }

cases.title: exports named like Object.prototype members get their signatures
cases.note: Any export can be an entrypoint (WR-12), so __proto__ and constructor are recorded like any other name (c2a review 4).
